**STEP 2 - Ruler:** White square plate, roughly 22 cm across (side-to-side, undistorted). Treating it as a dinner-plate-sized vessel of about 24 cm diameter gives an area of about 450 cm²; the plate's visible width is about 22-24 cm, so I use ~450 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** Roasted/fried potato pieces (about 6-7 chunks), with a light golden crust. No visible sauce or oil pool.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The potato pieces cover roughly 25% of the plate area (about 110 cm²), clustered in the right-center of the plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Pile height averages about 2.5 cm across the cluster (chunks are ~3-4 cm across, stacked). 110 cm² x 2.5 cm ≈ 275 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cooked potato chunks are dense, bread-like solids; use bulk density ~0.8 g/ml. 275 ml x 0.8 ≈ 220 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Fried/roasted potato ≈ 150 kcal/100 g (roasted in oil adds fat; plain boiled would be ~80). Using 150 kcal/100 g: 220 g → ~330 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Six to seven chunks of potato, each roughly 3-4 cm, totalling about 200-220 g, is plausible for a small serving. Energy of ~330 kcal is consistent with fried potatoes.

Estimated total: about 220 g, about 330 kcal.
